subject: FinServe dedicated capacity — performance follow-up & validation plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@finserve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinServe dedicated capacity — performance follow-up & validation plan

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on SLOs and validation for the Dedicated deployment.

Recap of requirements you confirmed on the call:
- Target first-token latency (TTFP) goal: p95 <= 350 ms for typical prompts (avg prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Sustained tail latency target: p95 <= 900 ms for full-response completion on sequences up to 512 tokens.
- Concurrent active sessions at peak: 45 concurrent streaming sessions (each streaming ~1 token every 120–200 ms).
- Reserved throughput need: baseline of 80 tokens/sec sustained with bursts up to 300 tokens/sec for short windows (minutes).
- Availability/DR: warm standby in us-west for failover; SLA expectations discussed separately.

What Redwood will validate during the Dedicated performance window:
1) SLO validation across three candidate GPU families: NVIDIA A10G, A100-40GB, and H100-80GB (we'll test latency, throughput, and memory fit).
2) Streaming behavior: measure first-token latency, steady-state per-token latency, and jitter with your streaming client at target concurrency.
3) KV cache and prefix caching impact using your prompt mixes — we'll run both cold-cache and warmed-cache passes.
4) Autoscaling/queueing effects at your burst profiles so we can recommend reserved throughput and safe burst headroom.

What we need from you to start a focused validation run:
- A representative traffic trace (1–2 hours) showing request timestamps, sequence lengths, and token emission patterns (streaming cadence).
- Peak concurrency window timing (when you see the 45 concurrent sessions historically).
- Sample prompt templates (redacted where necessary) and one synthetic workload generator script if available.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu (3/26): you share traffic trace + samples.
- Tue (3/31): Redwood runs internal bench matrix and shares preliminary results and recommended GPU/throughput sizing.
- Wed (4/1): 2-hour joint validation window with FinServe traffic profile on a sandbox Dedicated pool.

Attached: initial bench matrix template (finserve-slo-bench-matrix.xlsx) and our test plan draft (redwood-dedicated-test-plan.md).

Next step: can you share the traffic trace by EOD Thursday? If that timeline is tight, tell us which items we should prioritize.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServe dedicated capacity — performance follow-up & validation plan

Thanks Rachel — adding some engineering details and the validation matrix I propose so we can be explicit with FinServe on what each test will show.

High-level validation matrix (what we'll run in the sandbox Dedicated pool):
- GPU variants: A10G (cost-efficient), A100-40GB (balanced for medium contexts), H100-80GB (best latency for large contexts).
- Tests per GPU:
  * Cold-cache single-client latency (TTFP) at sequence lengths: 64 / 128 / 512 tokens.
  * Warm-cache steady-state streaming at concurrencies: 10 / 25 / 45 concurrent sessions. Measure per-token latency distribution and token drop/serialization behavior.
  * Burst throughput test: ramp to 300 tokens/sec for 5 min, observe queue depth and p95 latency.
  * Memory and batch sizing: find the largest batch size that keeps p95 TTFP under 350 ms while meeting throughput.

Minimum inputs I need from FinServe to make the matrix faithful:
- Distribution of sequence lengths (percentages for <=64, 65–256, 257–512).
- Median tokens emitted per streaming session and average inter-token time.
- Whether they use forced stop tokens or streaming truncation (affects KV cache behavior).

Cost / preliminary sizing note (ballpark):
- A10G: lowest hourly infra cost; expect higher p95 latency at +10–40% vs A100 for 512-token cases. Good for bursty workloads with shorter contexts.
- A100-40GB: best tradeoff for mixed context sizes; recommended as starting point for FinServe if they want predictable per-request latency and moderate cost.
- H100-80GB: recommended only if FinServe insists on the tightest p95 latency for long contexts and will accept higher infra cost.

I'll draft a short script to translate your traffic trace into our bench harness and include it in the Drive link. If Rachel can confirm we get the trace by 3/26, I can run the first pass on 3/31 and capture results for the 4/1 joint run.

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@finserve.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServe dedicated capacity — performance follow-up & validation plan

Rachel / Ben / Vanessa — thanks for the clear plan and matrix. Confirming we can deliver the following by tomorrow EOD (3/24):
- 90-minute anonymized trace (timestamps + sequence lengths + per-session token cadence). Attached as finserve_stream_trace_20260322.csv (redacted).
- Sequence length distribution: <=64: 48%, 65–256: 39%, 257–512: 13%.
- Typical streaming cadence: median inter-token 150 ms, bursts down to 90 ms in high-urgency flows.
- Peak concurrency: we typically see sustained 45 concurrent streaming sessions during end-of-day batch windows for some customers; peak bursts to ~70 for brief spikes (~30–60s).

A couple of clarifying asks from our side:
1) Can you provide a short cost delta estimate between A100 and A10G for the baseline sizing you recommend? We need the delta to justify the higher tier internally.
2) During the joint validation window, can we have read-only access to the raw latency logs so our infra team can run internal dashboards? (We expect you to redact any PII.)

We'll upload the trace and a small synthetic workload generator to the Drive link you shared. Looking forward to the first-pass numbers on 3/31.

Best,
Alex Harper
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
FinServe Inc.
alex.harper@finserve.com | +1 (617) 555-0126
